source.title: AI/semis evening brief, Oct 20: 65 updates, 23 high
source.body:
# Anthropic's IPO filing shows $16bn in half-year revenue and up to $750bn in planned compute spending

**The bottom line:** Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus and SpaceX's results both show AI lab revenue and compute budgets growing very fast. That spending is feeding straight into chips, memory and power. The weak link is the neoclouds, the leveraged middlemen that rent out GPUs. Their IPOs are stalling and Nvidia appears to be stepping in to support them.

## Anthropic's prospectus puts numbers on the AI arms race

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude models, had first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, according to its draft S-1 filing for an IPO ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmeu0824885.d.html)). Compute and infrastructure spending was nearly $9 billion, up from $2.3 billion. That already exceeds the $7.3 billion it spent on compute in all of 2025 ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510432?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The headline $80.7 billion net loss looks alarming. About $72 billion of it, however, is a mark-to-market charge on convertible notes, an accounting cost rather than cash burned ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510432?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). The bigger number is forward-looking. Anthropic may spend an additional $750 billion on compute over the coming years, including deals still being negotiated ([Bloomberg video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6OnuO6Y5OQY)). One such deal: Bloomberg reports Nscale, a European AI cloud firm, is in talks to sell Anthropic about $45 billion of computing power ([Bloomberg video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3MlgPZREVCw)).

**Read-through:** A single lab committing that much to compute supports demand visibility for Nvidia (NVDA), cloud providers and the memory and networking chain. It also concentrates risk. Much of that $750 billion is contingent and depends on revenue continuing to grow at this pace.

## SpaceX becomes an AI compute company, and wants its own fab

SpaceX (SPCX) reported Q3 revenue of $14.58 billion, up 161% and well ahead of the $12.87 billion consensus. AI revenue was $7.56 billion, now larger than its space business ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmeu0844539.d.html)). Capex was $19.59 billion, of which $16.44 billion went to AI. Backlog stood at $63 billion. The CFO said the company is on pace for $100 billion in annual recurring revenue by year-end ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmfa8006816.d.html)).

The most telling remark was about returns. The CFO said newly deployed compute pays back in under a year at current pricing, and that pricing is slightly above the top of the $30–50 per watt range the company gave last quarter. Musk said payback could shrink to six months next year ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510662?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). That directly contradicts the "AI overbuild" narrative, at least for operators with their own demand. Musk also argued that power, cooling and infrastructure, not chips, are now the binding constraints ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmeu0873441.d.html)).

Terafab, the chipmaking joint venture of SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA), now has a timeline:

- A first SRAM test chip at its Austin R&D centre around May–June 2027.
- Mass production in Q3 2028.

Musk himself said the schedule has "very large error bars" ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxrpa4766903.d.html)). US advanced logic fabs typically take three-plus years to build. He said ASML (ASML), the Dutch monopoly supplier of lithography tools, and other suppliers have accelerated equipment deliveries ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmfa8010861.d.html)). Korean media report Terafab is in talks with about 10 South Korean materials, components and equipment suppliers, several under NDA ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902194273.html)).

**Read-through:** This is incremental demand for equipment makers. It is also a long-dated threat to foundry concentration at TSMC, but only if execution matches the ambition.

## Neocloud cracks contrast with booming server demand

Not every link in the chain is healthy. Bloomberg reports neoclouds are losing favour. Neoclouds are the startups that borrowed heavily to buy GPUs and rent them out. South Korean AI computing supplier Elice fell 32% on its Seoul debut ([Bloomberg video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4WE0jaDsEns)). Australia's Firmus pulled its IPO this month and now seeks $2 billion-plus privately. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in it ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510465?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). The same report cites analysis that Nvidia has taken on over $170 billion of risk exposure to such customers through credit guarantees and debt help.

Singapore's DayOne Data Centers is reassessing a US IPO. It may delay the deal or halve it to $2.5–3 billion, from an original target of up to $5 billion at a $20 billion valuation ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510599?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Former PBOC governor Zhou Xiaochuan added a macro warning at the Bund Summit. Given the scale of AI capital flows, he said, some investments will fail and could trigger financial turmoil, so policymakers should stock up tools now ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901709630.html)).

Yet hardware demand shows no sign of cooling. Super Micro Computer (SMCI), which assembles AI server racks, raised fiscal Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5–19.5 billion from $14.5–15.5 billion. It also lifted gross margin guidance to 12.0–12.5% from 10.4–10.8% ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmev7633676.d.html)). The news lifted Dell (DELL) and HPE (HPE) too ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902445297.html)).

**Read-through:** The tension is between strong end-demand and fragile financing for the middle layer. Nvidia's role as financier of last resort is a growing risk to watch.

## Chips and memory: the equipment cycle extends to 2028

The fab buildout keeps accelerating. Industry group SEMI now forecasts record 2026 chip-equipment sales of $165.9 billion, up 23.2%, rising to $229.5 billion by 2028, a fifth straight year of growth ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuy4668415.d.html)). The same report notes:

- **TSMC (TSM):** raised 2026 capex to $60–64 billion from $52–56 billion.
- **ASML:** Q3 sales of €9.326 billion beat guidance and consensus, and it raised full-year guidance a second time.

TSMC's Q3 revenue rose 50.9% and net profit 68.7%, at a 66.4% gross margin. High-performance computing was 68% of revenue, and full-year growth guidance is now about 44% ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902386734.html)). A grim note: four workers died in a fall at TSMC's F22 fab construction site in Kaohsiung ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuy4804601.d.html)).

The squeeze is spreading upstream:

- **Equipment components:** Chinese outlet 36Kr describes "historic" price increases across the component chain, with pricing power shifting toward smaller parts makers. It flags valves, ceramics, RF power supplies and gas boxes ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4034867562255492)).
- **Argon:** liquid argon, a process gas, jumped 38–49% in China in under two weeks to ¥2,540–3,057 per ton. Low air-separation output collided with chip demand ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510516?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Germanium:** Yunnan Germanium (002428.SZ), a producer of the critical mineral used in optics and infrared, posted Q3 net profit up 2,642% to ¥102 million on revenue up 135% ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901532426.html)).

In memory, TrendForce expects Q4 DRAM contract prices to rise about 20% quarter on quarter. That is a deceleration from about 80% in Q2 and about 40% in Q3, though prices remain at high levels ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510491?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Korea's early-October data shows the boom in trade numbers. Chip exports jumped 222.5% year on year, helping total exports rise 123% to $61.6 billion ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuw7945337.d.html)). That benefits SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Samsung (005930.KS).

**Read-through:** The slowing price gains are the first hint the memory cycle may be maturing. Micron (MU) is holding a technology webinar on DRAM, HBM and NAND roadmaps ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213901979132.html)). Separately, its President and CTO Scott DeBoer sold about 28,500 shares at roughly $900 under a pre-set 10b5-1 trading plan ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723125/000156823826000003/0001568238-26-000003-index.htm)).

## Power and cooling: the real bottleneck shows up in the data

Musk's point about power shows up in the numbers:

- **China's grid:** data-centre electricity use rose 35.4% in September and 41.6% year to date, while total consumption grew just 1.2% ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510682?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Gas turbines:** global orders hit about 38GW in Q2, up 71% from 22GW, according to McCoy Power Reports. Full-year 2026 orders are seen above 100GW. That supports GE Vernova (GEV), Siemens Energy (ENR.DE) and Chinese parts suppliers ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510595?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Fuel cells:** solid oxide fuel cells are gaining attention because they can be deployed in modules and delivered quickly. Order conversion is still unproven ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510464?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

Inside the rack, the story is similar:

- **Vicor (VICR):** the maker of high-density power modules that feed AI processors grew Q3 revenue 78.5% ([Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/20/vicor-vicr-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- **Liquid cooling:** megawatt-scale systems are entering standardised mass delivery. One Chinese vendor won a single overseas order above ¥2.7 billion with a 120-day delivery cycle ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuw7904008.d.html)).
- **Capacitors:** Goldman Sachs research cited by CLS says MLCCs, the tiny ceramic capacitors on circuit boards, are now the third-largest cost in an AI server after GPUs and memory ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510590?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). That is supportive for Murata (6981.T) and Chinese peers.

## China: open-source inference, state data and humanoid robots

DeepSeek open-sourced its in-house inference framework, DeepInfer, along with a token codec. The release lets cloud providers run DeepSeek models at close to DeepSeek's own cost, and possibly below it ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901600750.html)). That further commoditises inference pricing.

Beijing registered China National Data Group, a central state-owned firm backed by the three telecom carriers and both state grids, to treat data as a factor of production for AI ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902410455.html)).

On robotics, Chinese suppliers of actuators, harmonic reducers and sensors are reportedly preparing capacity for Tesla's third-generation Optimus, which Tesla says is ready for mass production ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510437?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Reliability, cost and algorithm generalisation remain open hurdles. Momenta's CEO separately pointed to 2028 as the inflection point for scaled L4 autonomous driving ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510579?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

## What to watch

- **Anthropic's IPO:** the final S-1 terms, and whether the Nscale deal and other compute contracts are confirmed.
- **Supermicro earnings on Nov 3:** whether the margin uplift is durable.
- **Neocloud funding:** whether Nvidia's Firmus investment closes, and whether DayOne proceeds or shrinks its offering.
- **Memory pricing:** Micron's roadmap commentary, and whether Q4 DRAM gains fade further toward a peak.
- **Terafab:** supplier announcements from Korea and ASML that test the 2027–2028 timeline.

# China (30)

## AI (7)

🔴 **[10-21 08:45 Beijing] DeepSeek announces open-source inference framework DeepInfer and production-grade token codec; enables cloud providers to match DeepSeek official performance/costs**  
October 20: DeepSeek announced it is open-sourcing its internal inference framework "DeepInfer" and simultaneously releasing production-grade token encoding/decoding component deepseek-recipe. This allows cloud providers to deploy DeepSeek models using DeepSeek's native inference framework, achieving performance and costs close to DeepSeek's official calls. With proper load scheduling, large cloud providers' non-native DeepSeek deployment costs may even be lower than official native costs.  
_News · EastMoney · DeepSeek · [Source](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901600750.html)_

**[10-21 09:59 Beijing] Today AI raises cumulative $200m+ funding from IDG, Tencent, Sequoia and others**  
On October 21, Today AI announced it has cumulatively raised over $200 million in funding. Investors include IDG Capital, Tencent, Five Sources Capital, Ant Group, Sequoia China, Transsion, Tongguo Ventures and Shanghai Jiaotong University Hanyuan Assets.  
_News · Sina · Today AI · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuw8049042.d.html)_

**[10-21 09:58 Beijing] TSMC Q3 beats expectations; Scientific Innovation AI ETF up 2.8% on strong advanced process demand**  
TSMC Q3 revenue up 50.9% year-on-year, net profit up 68.7%, gross margin maintained at 66.4% high. High-performance computing (HPC) revenue reached 68% of total. Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to about 44%. Strong advanced process demand has injected strong momentum into the entire AI compute supply chain. As of 09:55 today, Scientific Innovation AI ETF Huatai Bailei (159139) surged 2.8%, with tracked Scientific Innovation AI index rising in tandem. By weight structure, electronics account for 52.18%, communications and computing each about 18%, media and defense industries combined about 8%.  
_News · EastMoney · TSMC · [Source](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902386734.html)_

**[10-21] China establishes National Data Group to advance data economy and support AI development**  
China launched China National Data Group Co. Ltd., a centrally administered state-owned enterprise tasked with developing and using the country's data resources. Backed by major state-owned telecom operators and power utilities, the wholly state-owned company represents Beijing's effort to treat data as a factor of production and support artificial intelligence development.  
_News · Caixin Global · [Source](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-10-21/china-creates-national-data-group-to-advance-data-economy-102495434.html)_

Given the massive capital flows to AI and related infrastructure, investment failures could trigger financial turmoil. He called for research and contingency planning to stock policy tools to address such disruptions and impacts.

_News · CLS · [Source](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510623?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)_

**[10-21 09:54 Beijing] China Electronics breakthrough in diamond heterojunction for wide-bandgap semiconductors**  
China Electronics' Industry Foundation Research Institute solid-state microwave devices and circuits national key lab diamond team achieved breakthroughs in diamond heterojunctions, creating the first cubic aluminum nitride/diamond heterojunction material and field-effect transistor. The team innovatively proposed domain-matched epitaxial growth mode, using diamond surface hydrogen termination as a reaction control platform to form high-quality single-crystal cubic aluminum nitride/diamond heterojunction, successfully developing high-performance enhancement-mode heterojunction field-effect transistors. This work completed critical connections from theoretical calculation to material preparation to device validation, providing material foundation for high-performance diamond RF devices. The heterojunction epitaxy method developed by the team provides a new paradigm for semiconductor material preparation. Next, the team will continue optimizing material and device processes, advancing heterojunction technology, and supporting next-generation ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor technology upgrades.  
_News · Sina · China Electronics · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuy4815161.d.html)_

**[10-21 08:08 Beijing] Semiconductor equipment orders remain robust; components experiencing historic full-chain price increases; pricing power shifting downstream**  
Global prosperity cycle confirmed; SEMI forecasts 2026 global semiconductor equipment sales record $165.9 billion, up 23.2% YoY. Growth expected to continue through 2028, totaling $229.5 billion, marking five consecutive years of growth. Global semiconductor equipment components experiencing historic full-chain price surge. Pricing power structurally shifting from chip terminal toward equipment and components. Component firms are smaller with high fixed-cost ratios; price increases directly convert to profit. Manufacturing expansion cycles stretch 12–18 months with minimal supply elasticity. Watch valve/pipe, ceramic, RF power supply, and gas box imports with extended delivery: domestic substitution and price-increase logic.
